subject: Eval -> Dedicated pool commit: proposed schedule & terms
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: J. Thompson <jthompson@acme.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Eval -> Dedicated pool commit: proposed schedule & terms

Hi JT —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I sketched a concise evaluation -> committed deployment path so Acme can validate latency/cost at production scale and get predictable capacity for Q1 feature launches. Attached: Acme_MAP_v1.pdf (plan + milestones) and GPU_Sizing_Table.xlsx (proposal).

High-level proposal (short):
- 4-week technical evaluation (week-of-dec to mid-dec): 2 x A100-40GB equivalent nodes for full-stack load tests (Redwood-managed hosted eval).
- Post-eval committed pool: Dedicated GPU pool sized at 8 x A100-40GB equivalent (sized for ~2000 concurrent inference tokens/min across peak flows).
- Term options: 12-month preferred at baseline pricing; alternative 9-month with a 5% step-up.
- Billing: committed capacity billed at $6.25/GPU-hour. Burst allowed up to 2.5x instantaneous capacity; burst usage billed at 1.5x committed rate ($9.38/GPU-hour). Monthly burst capped to 6% of committed hours (automatic throttling beyond cap).
- Ramp: 0–30 days: 25% of pool active; 31–60 days: 60%; 61–90 days: 100% (milestone-based payments & credits tied to MAP deliverables).
- SLA & credits: 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated; credits scale for sustained downtime per SLA schedule (we can detail in SOW).

Requested from Acme this week: confirmation of the 8-node sizing + preference on 9 vs 12-month term and whether you need a separate burst-cap bucket for peak inference jobs.

If that aligns, we can update the MAP, produce a draft order form, and send for legal review.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1.pdf (pdf, 110KB)]
[Attachment: GPU_Sizing_Table.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)]

From: J. Thompson <jthompson@acme.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: R. Patel <rpatel@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Eval -> Dedicated pool commit: proposed schedule & terms

Ava —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying Qs before we confirm:
1) Burst billing: when you say 1.5x committed rate for burst, is that applied per GPU-hour only while bursting, or do we get billed on the higher rate retroactively for the whole month if burst cap is exceeded?
2) The monthly burst cap at 6% — can we make that a daily allowance instead (e.g., up to 1.5 hours/day at 2.5x) for our scheduled nightly batch runs?
3) We prefer a shorter contract to start. Would Redwood do 9 months at a smaller uplift (3%) instead of 5% — because we're still validating cost curves in prod.
4) Do you have a SOC2 extract we can share with procurement?

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call this week to align.

—JT
J. Thompson
Head of MLOps, Acme AI
[Attachment: internal-storage-policy.pdf (pdf, 75KB)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme Qs on burst/term

Ava / Marissa — forwarding JT's questions. My suggested negotiation posture below:

- Burst billing: charge at 1.5x only for actual burst hours. If monthly burst cap (6%) is exceeded, we throttle automatically and notify customer; we do not retroactively charge the higher rate on non-burst hours. If Acme needs an overage policy, offer a capped overage credit + pre-buy option.
- Daily vs monthly cap: allow daily shaping for scheduled nightly batches: up to 2.5x for up to 2 hours/day, but keep an aggregate monthly cap (equivalent to ~6% of hours). This protects other tenants on shared infra and keeps predictability.
- Term: offer 9-month at +5% (internal guidance) but give sales the flexibility to approve +3% for strategic logos if legal signs off.
- SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 extract + customer-facing evidence bundle.

If we give them +3% for 9 months, we should ask for a slightly earlier payment schedule (net-30 prepayment on first month) and a signed MAP within 10 business days.

Sean

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: J. Thompson <jthompson@acme.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Eval -> Dedicated pool commit: proposed schedule & terms

JT — quick answers inline and a small concession to help you get to production faster.

1) Burst billing: billed only for actual burst hours at 1.5x committed rate. No retroactive uplift across non-burst hours.
2) Daily shaping: we can support a daily burst allowance for scheduled jobs — proposed: up to 2.5x for up to 2 hours/day with an aggregate monthly cap equal to 6% of committed hours. If you need additional predictable burst, we can offer a pre-purchased burst credit bucket.
3) Term & uplift: we can offer 9 months at +3% (i.e., $6.44/GPU-hour committed) provided we get a signed MAP and order form within 12 business days and first-month prepayment (or net-15 invoice).
4) SOC2: attached SOC2 extract and a short evidence packet.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm sizing (8-node pool) and accept the 9-month +3% option or tell us you want 12 months.
- We update MAP and send an order form + DocuSign link (I'll loop Marissa to own the order form).
- Internal kickoff scheduled for 1 week after signature; evaluation window can start earlier if you want hosted eval nodes.

If that sounds workable, I'll push the revised MAP and order form today.

Regards,
Ava
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-extract.zip (zip, 220KB)]

From: J. Thompson <jthompson@acme.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: R. Patel <rpatel@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Eval -> Dedicated pool commit: proposed schedule & terms

Ava —

Thanks. 9 months at +3% with the daily shaping sounds acceptable. We'll confirm sizing (8 nodes) by end of day tomorrow. A couple of asks before signature:
- Can Redwood include one month of build credits (20% credit on committed fees) to help with migration and spike testing?
- Can you add a clause that our nightly batch jobs are exempt from throttle up to the daily burst allowance (we need predictable results at 02:00 PST)?

If you can confirm those two, we'll aim to sign next week and start the eval immediately after.

—JT

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: J. Thompson <jthompson@acme.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Eval -> Dedicated pool commit: proposed schedule & terms

JT —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We can commit to the two asks:
1) One month of build credits = 20% credit applied to committed fees for month 1 (applied as invoice credit).
2) Nightly batch exemption: we'll include explicit language that scheduled nightly batch windows (specified in the MAP) are prioritized and exempt from throttling up to the daily burst allowance; any sustained overage beyond the daily allowance will invoke the aggregate cap and potential throttling.

I'll send the updated MAP + order form via DocuSign in the next hour for signature (HubSpot deal RW-ACME-2026-11 updated). Please route the signed DocuSign back to me and cc: legal@acme.ai.

Deliverables/schedule once signed:
- Day 0 (post-sign): order form executed, account team kickoff, provisioning window scheduled.
- Week 1: hosted eval nodes available (if requested).
- Weeks 2–6: ramp and load testing per MAP milestones.
- End of week 8: production-ready handoff and pool at 100% active.

Thanks — I’ll lock the DocuSign now.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://hubspot.com/deal/RW-ACME-2026-11]
